text.p: The following are the main stories from Thursday morning's Austrian newspapers:

- Austria's teachers union has threatened to call a strike should further austerity measures be applied to the educational sector. The government says it needs to to employ more teachers but is unable to raise spending.
- The merger of savings banks Die Erste and GiroCredit should be completed by the end of September.
- A 62-year old computer expert was arrested on suspicion of having penned letters claiming responsibility for a series of letter bombs.

- SBC Warburg forecasts in a study the fair swap rate between Bank Austria and Creditanstalt shares should be at around 1.15 Bank Austria shares for each Creditanstalt share. Bank Austria took over its closest competitor earlier this year.

- An unnamed insurer is said to be a new shareholder in Creditanstalt after insurance group EA-Generali sold its 4.8 percent stake. Switzerland's Winterthur Versicherung or Germany's Allianz are seen as the most likely candidates.
- The tender for Austria's third mobile phone network, due this summer, is expected to raise little more than one billion schillings for the government.

- Wolfgang Ruttenstorfer, secretary of state in the finance ministry, said national grid company Verbund and the country's regional energy providers should jointly take over a 25 percent stake in Upper Austriam energy provider OKA, which is due to be privatised.

- Chemicals group Donau Chemie's planned management buyout has been delayed after the group's owners, French chemicals group Rhone Poulenc and Creditanstalt, have run into difficulties with plans to sell pharmaceuticals unit Gerot.
- Bank Austria's workers council insists it will veto the the planned privatisation of the bank.

- Vienna's conservative party leader Bernhard Goerg says Germany's Westdeutsche Landesbank should take over part of the Bank Austria shares currently held by the City of Vienna's AVZ foundation and then immediately recall its first option to acquire further shares from AVZ.
- President Thomas Klestil says he wants to start an intensive public debate on whether Austria should join NATO.
- The government wants to earn some three billion schillings in extra revenues by lowering the duty-free allowance on cigarettes.
- Die Erste savings bank supervisory board chairman Herbert Schimetschek says the current debate about Westdeutsche Landesbank's first option on Bank Austria shares was "unprofessional".

- Engineering group Voest-Alpine Industrieanlagenbau, a unit of VA Technologie, plans to become a world leader in its sector after having invested more than one billion schillings in the reasearch and production of new products.
- Creditor protection agency KSV says it expects no major insolvencies this year.
